crypto.syllabus:
📘 UNIT - I: Overview of Network Security & Block Ciphers

MODULE 1
• Overview of Network Security OSI Security Architecture, Security Attacks, Security Services, Security Mechanisms, A Model for Network Security.
• Classical Encryption Techniques Symmetric Cipher Model, Substitution Techniques (Caesar, Playfair, Hill), Transposition Techniques, Rotor Machines, Steganography.
• Block Ciphers & DES Structure and Data Encryption Standard (DES), Strength of DES, Double and Triple DES, Block Cipher Modes: ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR.

📘 UNIT - II: AES, Stream Ciphers & Public-Key Cryptography

MODULE 2
• Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Origins, Structure, Round Functions (SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey), AES Key Expansion.
• Stream Ciphers & PRNG Principles, Block Cipher based PRNG, RC4 Stream Cipher architecture.
• Public-Key Cryptography Principles of Asymmetric Cryptosystems, RSA Algorithm, Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange, Key Management and Distribution, X.509 Certificates.

📘 UNIT - III: Hash Functions, Digital Signatures & System Security

MODULE 3
• Cryptographic Hash Functions & MAC Applications, SHA and MD5 Algorithms, HMAC, CMAC, Digital Signatures (NIST DSA).
• Transport & Network Security SSL/TLS, HTTPS, SSH, E-Mail Security (PGP, S/MIME), IP Security (IPsec: AH, ESP, IKE).
• System Security & Firewalls Intruders, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), Password Management, Virus and Countermeasures, Firewall Design Principles and Types.

📚 Recommended Textbooks & Reference Books

REFERENCES
1. William Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security – Principles and Practice (6th Edition).
2. Douglas R. Stinson, Cryptography Theory and Practice.
3. Joseph Migga Kizza, A Guide to Computer Network Security.

  5. Discourse Shift & Sentence Emotions: [Application & Synthesis] Discuss Emotion Classification at the sentence level and analyze how discourse markers (e.g., 'but', 'however') shift sentence sentiment.

📘 UNIT - I: Scalability Foundations & Microservices Architecture

MODULE 1
• Scalability Principles Vertical vs. Horizontal scaling, The AKF Scale Cube (X, Y, Z axis scaling), Stateless vs. Stateful services, CAP Theorem and PACELC Theorem.
• Microservices Design Decomposing monoliths, Service discovery, API Gateways, Inter-service communication (REST, gRPC, Event-Driven Messaging with Kafka/RabbitMQ).

📘 UNIT - II: Distributed Data Management & Caching

MODULE 2
• Distributed Storage & Partitioning Database Sharding, Consistent Hashing, Replication strategies (Master-Slave, Multi-Master, Leaderless / Dynamo-style).
• Caching Architectures Caching patterns (Cache-Aside, Write-Through, Write-Behind), Distributed Caching (Redis, Memcached), Content Delivery Networks (CDN).

📘 UNIT - III: Reliability, Concurrency & Stream Processing

MODULE 3
• High Availability & Fault Tolerance Circuit Breaker pattern, Rate Limiting, Bulkhead pattern, Chaos Engineering, Distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Jaeger).
• Distributed Stream Processing Batch vs. Stream processing, Event Sourcing, CQRS, Real-time data pipelines (Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, Apache Spark Streaming).

📚 Recommended Textbooks & Reference Books

REFERENCES
1. Martin Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems, O’Reilly.
2. Sam Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems (2nd Edition), O’Reilly.
3. Mark Richards and Neal Ford, Fundamentals of Software Architecture, O’Reilly.

stat_inference.syllabus:
📘 UNIT - I: Estimation Theory, Methods of Estimation & Resampling

MODULE 1
• Estimation Theory Basic concepts to estimation; Criteria for good estimator: Unbiasedness, consistency, efficiency, sufficiency, Cramer-Rao inequality, Rao-Blackwell theorem, Fisher Information, Lehmann-Scheffé theorem, Simple Problems on UMVUE.
• Methods of Estimation Method of Moments (MoM), Least Squares, and Maximum Likelihood (MLE), Properties and Simple problems.
• Resampling Methods Jackknife, Bootstrap, Estimation of bias and standard deviation of point estimation by Jackknife & Bootstrap methods with examples, U-statistic, Kernel and examples.
• Interval Estimation Confidence level, Confidence Intervals using pivots, and shortest length confidence interval.

📘 UNIT - II: Testing of Hypotheses & Non-Parametric Tests

MODULE 2
• Testing of Hypotheses Concepts of testing, Statistical Hypothesis, Simple & Composite hypotheses, Null & Alternative hypotheses, Type-I & Type-II errors, Critical region, Level of significance, Power of test, Most Powerful (MP) test, Uniformly Most Powerful (UMP) test, Neyman-Pearson Lemma, Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT).
• Sequential Analysis Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) with examples.
• Non-Parametric Tests Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test for one & two samples, Kendall’s Tau test, Kruskal-Wallis test, Friedman test, Ansari-Bradley test.

📘 UNIT - III: Non-Parametric Density Estimation, Simulation & Bayesian Inference

MODULE 3
• Non-Parametric Density Estimation Rosenblatt’s Naïve Estimator, Kernel Density Estimator (KDE) and its properties, Consistency and Mean Squared Error (MSE).
• Simulation Techniques Random number generation, Inverse transform method, Generating random variables from Exponential, Poisson, and Normal distributions using Box-Muller Transformation.
• Bayesian Inference Prior and Posterior distributions, Conjugate priors, Loss and Risk functions, Bayes estimators under squared error loss, MCMC (Markov Chain Monte Carlo) methods: Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm and Gibbs Sampler.

📚 Recommended Textbooks & Reference Books

REFERENCES
1. V.K. Rohatgi and A.K. Md. E. Saleh, An Introduction to Probability and Statistics (3rd Edition), John Wiley & Sons.
2. G. Casella and R.L. Berger, Statistical Inference (2nd Edition), Duxbury Press.
3. E.J. Dudewicz and S.N. Mishra, Modern Mathematical Statistics, John Wiley & Sons.
4. J.D. Gibbons and S. Chakraborti, Nonparametric Statistical Inference (5th Edition), CRC Press.
5. B.W. Silverman, Density Estimation for Statistics and Data Analysis, Chapman & Hall.
6. C.P. Robert and G. Casella, Monte Carlo Statistical Methods (2nd Edition), Springer.

SECTION I: COMPREHENSIVE IMPORTANT QUESTIONS LIST (UNIT-WISE)

UNIT-I: Estimation Theory, Methods of Estimation & Resampling

CORE ESTIMATION
Part A: Fundamental Concepts (Short Answer – 2 Marks)
  1. State the criteria for a good point estimator and define unbiasedness with an example.
  2. Define Fisher Information and write its mathematical expression for a single parameter.
  3. Define the U-statistic and state its core objective in estimation.
  4. Explain the main difference between the Jackknife and Bootstrap resampling methods.
  5. Define confidence interval and explain the concept of a pivot (pivotal quantity).
Part B: Higher-Order Thinking (Application & Analysis – 12 Marks)
  1. Cramer-Rao Inequality: State and prove the Cramer-Rao Inequality. Explain the conditions under which the lower bound of variance is achieved.
  2. Rao-Blackwell Theorem: State and prove the Rao-Blackwell Theorem. Explain how it is used to improve an unbiased estimator using a sufficient statistic.
  3. Lehmann-Scheffé Theorem: State and prove the Lehmann-Scheffé Theorem. Explain its application in constructing a Uniformly Minimum Variance Unbiased Estimator (UMVUE).
  4. Poisson Estimation (MLE & MoM): Derive the Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE) and Method of Moments Estimator (MME) for the parameter θ of a Poisson distribution, and analyze their properties.
  5. Normal Parameters Estimation: Derive the Maximum Likelihood Estimators for the parameters μ and σ² of a Normal distribution N(μ, σ²).
  6. Jackknife Algorithm: Describe the algorithm to estimate the bias and standard deviation of a point estimator using the Jackknife method.
  7. Bootstrap Resampling: Explain the non-parametric Bootstrap algorithm for estimating the variance of a point estimator.
  8. Shortest Length CI: Explain the method of constructing the shortest length confidence interval for a parameter with a suitable example.

UNIT-II: Testing of Hypotheses & Non-Parametric Tests

HYPOTHESIS TESTING
Part A: Fundamental Concepts (Short Answer – 2 Marks)
  1. Define Most Powerful (MP) test and Uniformly Most Powerful (UMP) test.
  2. State the fundamental concept and stopping rule of the Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT).
  3. State the test statistic and null hypothesis for the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
  4. Describe the main objective of Kendall’s Tau (τ) rank correlation coefficient.
  5. Explain the basic purpose and conditions for using the Kruskal-Wallis test.
Part B: Higher-Order Thinking (Analysis & Evaluation – 12 Marks)
  1. Neyman-Pearson Lemma: State and prove the Neyman-Pearson Lemma for testing a simple null hypothesis against a simple alternative hypothesis.
  2. UMP Test Construction: Demonstrate how to construct a Uniformly Most Powerful (UMP) test for testing H₀: θ = θ₀ against H₁: θ > θ₀ in a single-parameter Exponential family distribution.
  3. Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT): Explain the Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) procedure and discuss its asymptotic properties and test statistic distribution.
  4. SPRT Decision Boundaries: Derive the Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) boundaries A and B for testing simple hypotheses, and evaluate their relation to Type I and Type II errors (α and β).
  5. Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) Test: Explain the procedure, test statistic, and decision criteria for the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test.
  6. Kruskal-Wallis Test: Outline the test procedure for the Kruskal-Wallis test for k independent samples and evaluate its performance against standard ANOVA.
  7. Friedman Test: Explain the test procedure and calculation steps for the Friedman test for randomized complete block designs.
  8. Ansari-Bradley Test: Explain the Ansari-Bradley test for comparing the scale parameters (dispersion) of two independent distributions.

UNIT-III: Non-Parametric Density Estimation, Simulation & Bayesian Methods

BAYES & MCMC
Part A: Fundamental Concepts (Short Answer – 2 Marks)
  1. Define Rosenblatt’s Naïve Density Estimator.
  2. What is a conjugate prior family? Give an example of a conjugate prior pair.
  3. Define Priori and Posteriori distributions in Bayesian inference.
  4. State the main purpose of the MCMC (Markov Chain Monte Carlo) framework.
  5. Explain the inverse transform method for generating random numbers from a continuous uniform distribution.
Part B: Higher-Order Thinking (Application & Synthesis – 12 Marks)
  1. Rosenblatt Estimator Properties: Derive the mathematical expression for the bias and variance of Rosenblatt’s Naïve Density Estimator.
  2. KDE Consistency & MSE: Prove the consistency of Kernel Density Estimators and derive the Mean Squared Error (MSE) expression.
  3. Random Variate Generation: Explain algorithms for generating random variates from Exponential and Poisson distributions.
  4. Box-Muller Transformation: Formulate an algorithm to generate random variables from a Normal distribution using the Box-Muller transformation, and explain how to assess the reliability of generated random numbers.
  5. Bayesian Parameter Estimation: Describe the procedure for obtaining the Bayesian point estimator of a parameter under a squared error loss function given a conjugate prior.
  6. Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm: Formulate and detail the step-by-step implementation of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm for sampling from a target posterior distribution.
  7. Gibbs Sampler: Explain the Gibbs Sampler algorithm for multi-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation and compare it with the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm.

opt_tech.syllabus:
📘 UNIT - I: Linear Programming, Duality & Simplex Methods

MODULE 1
• Linear Programming Foundations Convex sets, Mathematical formulation of LPP, Graphical solution method, Extreme points, Feasible solutions, Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming.
• Simplex Algorithms Standard form of LPP, Slack and Surplus variables, Simplex algorithm, Charnes’ Big-M method (Method of Penalties), Two-Phase Simplex method, Degeneracy and cycling in LPP.
• Duality Theory Formulation of Dual problem, Primal-Dual relationships, Fundamental Duality Theorem, Weak Duality Theorem, Complementary Slackness theorem, Dual Simplex algorithm.

📘 UNIT - II: Transportation, Assignment & Sequencing Problems

MODULE 2
• Transportation Problem (TPP) Mathematical formulation, Balanced & Unbalanced problems, Initial Basic Feasible Solution (IBFS) via North-West Corner, Least Cost, and Vogel’s Approximation Method (VAM), Optimality test using MODI (u-v) method, Degeneracy resolution.
• Assignment Problem (AP) Mathematical model, Hungarian Assignment method, Unbalanced assignment, Prohibited assignments, Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP).
• Job Sequencing Processing n jobs through 2 machines, Processing n jobs through 3 machines using Johnson’s algorithm, Processing 2 jobs through m machines.

📘 UNIT - III: Integer Programming, Network Analysis & Queuing Theory

MODULE 3
• Integer Linear Programming (ILPP) Gomory’s Cutting Plane method for Pure and Mixed ILPP, Branch and Bound technique.
• Network Analysis (CPM & PERT) Project network representation, Critical Path Method (CPM), Early and Late event times, Floats (Total, Free, Independent), Project Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT), Probability of project completion, Time-Cost Trade-Off (Crashing).
• Queuing Theory Queuing system characteristics, Kendall’s notation, Birth-Death processes, Steady-state solutions of (M/M/1):(∞/FIFO) and (M/M/1):(N/FIFO) queuing models, Little’s formula.

📚 Recommended Textbooks & Reference Books

1. Kanti Swarup, P.K. Gupta, and Man Mohan, Operations Research, Sultan Chand & Sons.
2. Hamdy A. Taha, Operations Research: An Introduction (10th Edition), Pearson.
